prompt: Enum.valueOf explodes on unknown text, so wrap it: parse a log level safely with a fallback, compare levels by their declaration order, and find the highest level in a list of tokens.
explanation: valueOf matches the constant name exactly, so real input has to be trimmed and upper-cased first, and the IllegalArgumentException it throws for anything unrecognised is what a try/catch turns into a harmless fallback (an empty string is just another unknown name). Every enum implements Comparable using declaration order, so compareTo >= 0 is a clean "this level or more severe" test. highest reuses both helpers and keeps a running best, starting from the lowest constant.
hints: Handle the null text before you touch valueOf, then call LogLevel.valueOf(text.trim().toUpperCase()) inside a try block.
Catch IllegalArgumentException and return the fallback from the catch block -- that also covers the empty string.
highest can start with LogLevel.TRACE and loop, calling parseOrDefault with TRACE as the fallback so unparseable tokens can never raise the result.
